input_scope: Only actual anonymous statement/approved definition contexts and genuine independent blind reconstruction. No proof/module/authored publication context/previous verdicts or repairs.

lean.statement:
∀ {d : ℕ} (hd : 2 ≤ d)
    {κ : ℝ} (hκ : 2 ≤ κ)
    (O : Matrix.orthogonalGroup (Fin d) ℝ),
    let θ : Fin d → ℝ := fun i => ((i.val : ℝ) + 1 / 2) * Real.pi / (d : ℝ)
    let A : Matrix (Fin d) (Fin d) ℝ :=
      (O : Matrix (Fin d) (Fin d) ℝ) *
        Matrix.diagonal (fun i => (κ + 1) / 2 + (κ - 1) / 2 * Real.cos (θ i)) *
        (O : Matrix (Fin d) (Fin d) ℝ).transpose
    A.PosDef ∧ (A - 1).PosSemidef ∧
      (κ • (1 : Matrix (Fin d) (Fin d) ℝ) - A).PosSemidef
approved_definition_context: Fin d is the finite coordinate set indexed from zero. A finitely supported function Fin d to real represents an arbitrary real coordinate vector because the domain is finite.

Matrix.orthogonalGroup (Fin d) real is the full real orthogonal group with either determinant sign. Both products with its transpose equal the identity; membership does not supply a probability law or algorithmic access.

Matrix.diagonal uses the displayed values on the diagonal and zero elsewhere. Matrix multiplication and transpose are their usual finite-coordinate operations. The matrix numeral1 is the identity matrix; • is real scalar multiplication of matrices. Addition/subtraction are matrix operations, not comparisons between individual entries.

Matrix.PosSemidef M means M is Hermitian and the real quadratic form is nonnegative on every finitely supported coordinate vector. Matrix.PosDef M means Hermitian and strictly positive on every nonzero such vector. Over real entries Hermitian is symmetry. These are propositions about the matrices, not additional arguments.

Real.pi/Real.cos and natural-to-real casts have their usual meanings. Real division is totalized at zero; that convention alone does not prove a denominator is nonzero. Conjunction asserts every displayed proposition at the same arguments.

blind_reconstruction.assumptions: Only d >= 2, kappa >= 2, and orthogonality of O. No determinant-sign restriction, no input positivity assertion on A or diagonal entries, and no probability law or algorithmic-access assumption on O.
blind_reconstruction.conclusion: A is real symmetric positive definite; A - I_d and kappa I_d - A are real symmetric positive semidefinite. Equivalently, I_d <= A <= kappa I_d in quadratic-form order, together with the explicitly asserted positive definiteness of A.
blind_reconstruction.constant_dependencies: No hidden, existential, asymptotic or unspecified constants. The scalar coefficients in lambda_i depend on kappa and the literal constants 1 and 2; theta_i depends on i and d and pi; the matrix depends on d, kappa and O. The identity bounds have literal lower scalar 1 and upper scalar kappa.
blind_reconstruction.domains: d is a natural number; kappa is real; indices are Fin d, represented by integers 0 through d-1; O belongs to the full real orthogonal group on Fin d; A and all matrices in the conclusion are real d-by-d matrices; x ranges over all of R^d.
blind_reconstruction.objects: Natural dimension d; real parameter kappa; real orthogonal d-by-d matrix O; real angles theta_i; real diagonal entries lambda_i; diagonal matrix D with entries lambda_i; constructed matrix A = O D O^T; identity matrix I_d; arbitrary real coordinate vectors x.
blind_reconstruction.quantifiers: Universally for every d with d >= 2, every real kappa with kappa >= 2, and every O in the full real orthogonal group. The angles and A are local definitions within this scope. Positive semidefiniteness quantifies universally over all coordinate vectors; positive definiteness quantifies over all nonzero coordinate vectors.
blind_reconstruction.reconstructed_theorem_text:
For every natural number d with d >= 2, every real number kappa with kappa >= 2, and every real d-by-d orthogonal matrix O, define, for each index i in {0, 1, ..., d-1},
    theta_i = (i + 1/2) pi / d,
    lambda_i = (kappa + 1)/2 + ((kappa - 1)/2) cos(theta_i),
and define
    A = O diag(lambda_0, ..., lambda_(d-1)) O^T.
Here O ranges over the full real orthogonal group: O O^T = O^T O = I_d, with either determinant sign permitted. The index i and the dimension d are cast to real numbers in the formula for theta_i. Every displayed division in these formulas is real division. In particular, 1/2 is the real number one-half, not a natural-number quotient; the exact literal grid is (i + 1/2) pi / d. The assumption d >= 2 ensures that its real denominator d is nonzero.

Then A is symmetric positive definite, A - I_d is symmetric positive semidefinite, and kappa I_d - A is symmetric positive semidefinite, all at the same d, kappa, and O. Explicitly, A = A^T; for every nonzero x in R^d, x^T A x > 0; for every x in R^d, x^T (A - I_d) x >= 0 and x^T (kappa I_d - A) x >= 0. The two latter matrices are symmetric as part of their positive-semidefinite assertions. Equivalently, the bounds are I_d <= A <= kappa I_d in quadratic-form order: for every x in R^d, x^T x <= x^T A x <= kappa x^T x. These are matrix quadratic-form bounds, not comparisons of individual entries.

All real coordinate vectors are covered; finite support adds no restriction because the coordinate set is finite. Positivity is an asserted output for the constructed matrices, not an input assumption on A or on the diagonal values. The only input restrictions are d >= 2, kappa >= 2, and membership of O in the full orthogonal group. The statement makes no probabilistic, distributional, sampling, or algorithmic assertion about O. There are no existential or hidden constants: the displayed coefficients depend only on kappa and the literal numerical constants, theta_i depends only on i and d, and A depends on d, kappa, and O through the displayed construction. The assertions hold for every allowed triple (d, kappa, O), without any further hypotheses.
blind_reconstruction.scopes: All three conjuncts concern the same locally defined A and the same d, kappa, O. Matrix order is quadratic-form order, not entrywise order. Matrix numeral 1 is I_d and scalar multiplication by kappa is real scalar matrix multiplication. The full orthogonal group permits both determinant signs. The exact grid is theta_i = ((real)i + 1/2) pi / ((real)d), with real addition, multiplication and division; it is not a grid produced by natural-number division. The finite coordinate domain means finitely supported vectors cover every coordinate vector. Although real division is totalized at zero, d >= 2 separately supplies d != 0.
